layers.authority: WA Department of Planning, Lands and Heritage (Aboriginal Lands Permit System), under the AAPA Regulations
layers.process: Entry or transit permits are needed for proclaimed Aboriginal Lands Trust reserves; the Minister can revoke them at any time. Some lands (such as Ngaanyatjarra) need their own council's permit too.

sources.title: Apply for a permit to access or travel through Aboriginal land

zone-requirements.note: The lead time is a planning buffer, not a published processing time.

own_names: Each community and native title corporation uses its own names; they come through the permit consultation.
culture-and-protocol.welcome_and_acknowledgement: Permits are granted only after consultation and in line with the wishes of the Aboriginal inhabitants. Some native title holders also require their own visitor's pass.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: Read each reserve's special conditions and any conditions set by communities along your route.
culture-and-protocol.photography_and_story_permissions: Not set out on the state page: ask the community or native title corporation before photographing or recording.
culture-and-protocol.reciprocity_and_gifts: Some communities charge to enter or camp on their land.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: The communities and native title corporations; the Aboriginal Lands Trust acts on their wishes, and the Department of Planning, Lands and Heritage runs the permit system.
culture-and-protocol.source: Government of Western Australia permit page

closures: The Minister can revoke a transit permit at any time; communities set their own conditions. Ask each community about closures for ceremony or sorry business.
culture-cycles.note: No closure calendar is published on the state page.
